epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per order with order number, date and total amount including VAT, excludes cancelled orders, and uses the file name orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet.

features.description: Customer capability to download a CSV file of their paid orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer is on their account page, When they trigger the order export, Then a CSV file is downloaded to their device.
Given a customer triggers the order export, When the download completes, Then the file contains only that customer's paid orders.
stories.aiReadyReason: The trigger location, the download behavior and the restriction to the customer's own paid orders are defined, so a developer can implement it without further input.
stories.description: An export action is available on the customer account page. Triggering it downloads a CSV file containing the customer's paid orders. Only the trigger and download behavior are covered here; the file content and file name are covered by other stories.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases

tasks.description: Add an export control on the customer account page that starts the export. Expected result: the control is visible to the customer and triggers the export request.
tasks.title: Add export action to account page

tasks.description: Create a backend endpoint that retrieves the authenticated customer's paid orders and returns them as a CSV download. Expected result: the endpoint returns a downloadable file containing only that customer's paid orders.
tasks.title: Create export endpoint for paid orders

tasks.description: Write tests checking that the account page action downloads a CSV file with only the customer's paid orders. Expected result: tests pass for the nominal case.
tasks.title: Verify download behavior

stories.title: Download paid orders as CSV from the account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer has paid orders, When they export their orders, Then the file contains exactly one row per paid order.
Given a row in the exported file, When it is read, Then it shows the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT of that order.
stories.aiReadyReason: Which delimiter (comma or semicolon) and which encoding should the CSV file use?
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from the account page
stories.description: The CSV contains one row per paid order. Each row includes the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. The delimiter and the encoding of the file are not decided yet, so the exact serialization of the rows cannot be finalized.
stories.iWant: each paid order listed as one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can see the key data of each order in my export

tasks.description: Read the order number, order date and total amount including VAT for each paid order of the customer. Expected result: the data set contains one record per paid order.
tasks.title: Retrieve paid order data

tasks.description: Build the CSV rows from the order data. Blocked: the delimiter and encoding are not decided, so this sub-task cannot be finalized until the PO answers the open question.
tasks.title: Serialize orders to CSV rows

tasks.description: Write tests verifying one row per paid order with order number, date and total including VAT. Expected result: tests pass once the format is decided.
tasks.title: Test row content

stories.title: Export one row per paid order with number, date and total including VAT

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer has a cancelled order, When they export their orders, Then the cancelled order does not appear in the file.
Given a customer has a paid order that is not cancelled, When they export their orders, Then that order appears in the file.
stories.aiReadyReason: The exclusion rule for cancelled orders is explicitly defined and can be verified with test data.
dependencies: Export one row per paid order with number, date and total including VAT
stories.description: Cancelled orders are not included in the exported file. All other paid orders remain included as defined in the export story.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the file only contains orders that count as paid

tasks.description: Apply a filter in the order query so that cancelled orders are excluded from the export. Expected result: no cancelled order is returned for the export.
tasks.title: Filter out cancelled orders

tasks.description: Write tests with a cancelled and a non-cancelled paid order. Expected result: only the non-cancelled order is exported.
tasks.title: Test cancelled order exclusion

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from the export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer exports on a given date, When the file is downloaded, Then its name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
Given a downloaded export file, When its name is checked, Then the file extension is .csv.
stories.aiReadyReason: Does the YYYY-MM-DD part of the file name refer to the export date or to another date?
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from the account page
stories.description: The downloaded file name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The specification does not state which date the YYYY-MM-DD part refers to.
stories.iWant: the exported file to be named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
stories.soThat: I can identify my export by its date

tasks.description: Set the download file name using the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Blocked: the date used in the name is not defined, so the final value cannot be determined.
tasks.title: Generate file name

tasks.description: Write a test checking the file name of the download against the pattern. Expected result: the name matches the defined pattern once the date is decided.
tasks.title: Test file name

stories.title: Name the exported file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
